details: CONFIRMED by reading: the clause is in the queue item's What and absent from all three texts (git diff

on a case the owner meets on an ordinary Russian keyboard (а, в, с all have Latin twins in shape).

git diff master...HEAD -- rules plugins -> "+  Never options that only differ in wording. Letters are Latin a, b, c
in every language; an answer in the owner's alphabet counts the same (Cyrillic а = a, б = b, в = c)." (same in

failing_case: The queue item's What (the owner's decision "a", which the brief says to build exactly) reads: "...an answer in
the owner's alphabet counts the same (Cyrillic а = a, б = b, в = c; a look-alike letter is read by its position
in the owner's alphabet only when the reply is in that alphabet)". The shipped sentence in rules/working-with-me.md:16,
rules/front.md:23 and plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:63 stops at "(Cyrillic а = a, б = b, в = c)." The
look-alike clause is missing. Live case it decides: options a, b, c; the owner, on a Russian keyboard, answers
"В" (Cyrillic ve, shaped like Latin B) or "с" (Cyrillic es, the key labelled C, shaped like Latin c). The rule
now gives no way to choose between reading the letter by its shape (b, c) and by its place in the alphabet
(c, none). The owner's clause settles this; the text does not.
fix_hint: Extend the parentheses in all three texts: "(Cyrillic а = a, б = b, в = c; a look-alike letter is read by its
position in the owner's alphabet only when the reply is in that alphabet)", then run
